The purpose of this policy is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### 🎯 Purpose & Scope
The purpose of Policy 50010 is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏳ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service as follows:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
- **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

### ✅ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval **at least two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

## 📄 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed to **provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.**[1]

---

### Eligibility (Scope)
This policy **applies to all regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment.**[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period.**[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches the maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation.**[1]

---

### Claim Process
Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days.**[1]

---

> ⚠️ *Please note that this information is based on HR policy documents and does not constitute legal advice. If you have specific questions about your situation, please consult with HR directly.*

The purpose of this policy is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

Here is a comprehensive overview of the full-time **Paid Time Off (PTO)** policy:

---

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### Purpose & Scope
The purpose of Policy 50010 is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏳ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, as follows:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |

PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual **stops** when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

> 💡 **Note:** If you are a part-time employee, a separate policy — **Policy 50020 (Types of Leave: Paid Time Off – Part-time)** — applies to you. Feel free to ask if you'd like details on that policy as well.

### 📄 Policy 50020 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) - Part-Time

**Purpose & Scope:** This policy establishes the Paid Time Off (PTO) guidelines for eligible part-time employees. It applies to all **regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week** and have completed their probationary period.[1]

---

#### ⏱️ PTO Accrual
Part-time employees accrue PTO on a **pro-rated basis** calculated from their regularly scheduled hours. The accrual rates are:

Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. **PTO is deducted in hourly increments**, and requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[1]

Part-time employees may **carry over up to 20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

Part-time employees who **transition to full-time status** will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy (Policy 50010).[1]

Here is a detailed side-by-side comparison of the Full-Time and Part-Time PTO policies:

---

## 📋 PTO Policy Comparison: Full-Time vs. Part-Time

| Category | **Full-Time** (Policy 50010) | **Part-Time** (Policy 50020) |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | Regular full-time employees who completed probationary period | Regular part-time employees working **min. 20 hrs/week** who completed probationary period |
| **Accrual Method** | Fixed days per year (per-pay-period basis) | Pro-rated hours per hour worked |
| **Accrual Rates** | See table below | See table below |
| **Carryover** | Up to **40 hours** per year | Up to **20 hours** per year |
| **Max Balance** | **240 hours** | Not specified (accrual stops at max) |
| **PTO Usage** | Vacation, personal time, illness, or any purpose | Must align with regular schedule; deducted in **hourly increments** |
| **Request Process** | Via designated time-off system; 3+ consecutive days need supervisor approval **2 weeks in advance** | Via time-off system |
| **PTO at Separation** | Paid out up to **80 hours** at current pay rate | Not specified |
| **Status Change** | N/A | PTO balance converted upon transition to full-time |

---

### 📅 Accrual Rate Details

#### Full-Time — Policy 50010
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
- **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
- **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
- **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
- **11+ years:** 30 days per year

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

#### Part-Time — Policy 50020
Part-time employees accrue PTO on a pro-rated basis calculated from their regularly scheduled hours. Accrual rates are:
- **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
- **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
- **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked[2]

---

### 🔑 Key Differences Highlighted

1. **Accrual Structure:** Full-time employees earn a fixed number of days per year, while part-time employees earn PTO proportionally based on hours actually worked.
2. **Carryover:** Full-time employees may carry over up to **40 hours**[1], whereas part-time employees may only carry over up to **20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year.[2]
3. **Separation Payout:** Full-time employees who separate in good standing are paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1] No equivalent payout provision is specified for part-time employees under Policy 50020.
4. **Seniority Tiers:** Full-time has **four** tenure tiers (0–2, 3–5, 6–10, 11+), while part-time has **three** tiers (0–2, 3–5, 6+).
5. **Status Change:** Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

The policy that covers time away from work when you are **temporarily unable to work** is **Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability**. Here is a summary of the key details:

---

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed **to provide income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability**.[1]

---

### Scope & Eligibility
This policy applies to **all regular full-time employees who have completed 90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

---

### How to File a Claim
Employees must:
1. **Notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability.
2. Submit a **completed claim form and supporting medical documentation** to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]

---

> ⚠️ *Please note that this is a general policy overview and does not constitute legal advice. For specific guidance related to your situation, please contact Human Resources directly.*

---

## 📋 Policy 10000 — Code of Ethics and Related Matters

### 🎯 Purpose
The purpose of Policy 10000 is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

---

### 👥 Scope
This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

---

### ✅ Standards of Conduct
All employees are expected to conduct themselves with integrity, honesty, and professionalism in all business dealings. Employees must avoid conflicts of interest and disclose any potential conflicts to their supervisor or the Ethics Committee.[1]

---

### ⚠️ Conflicts of Interest
Employees must not engage in activities that conflict with the interests of the organization. This includes:
- Financial interests in competing businesses
- Accepting gifts from vendors exceeding **$25 in value**
- Using company resources for personal gain[1]

---

### 📣 Reporting Violations
Employees who become aware of violations of this Code of Ethics are encouraged to report them through the **Ethics Hotline** or directly to the **Ethics Committee**. Reports may be made **anonymously**. The organization prohibits retaliation against employees who report violations in good faith.[1]

---

### 🔍 Compliance and Enforcement
Violations of this Code of Ethics may result in disciplinary action, up to and including **termination of employment**. The Ethics Committee is responsible for investigating reported violations and recommending appropriate corrective action.[1]

---

> 💡 **Note:** This policy falls under the **Governance** category and is currently **Active**. If you have further questions about specific sections or related policies, feel free to ask!

# 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

## Purpose & Scope

The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have **completed their probationary period**.[1]

---

## 📅 PTO Accrual

Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a **per-pay-period basis**:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|-----------------|-------------------|
| 0–2 years       | 15 days           |
| 3–5 years       | 20 days           |
| 6–10 years      | 25 days           |
| 11+ years       | 30 days           |
[1]

---

## 🗓️ PTO Usage

PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval **at least two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

## 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance

Employees may **carry over up to 40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops once this maximum is reached.[1]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

Employees who **separate from employment in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a **maximum of 80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

> **Note:** If you have questions about the Part-Time PTO policy, that is covered under a separate **Policy 50020**. Please let me know if you'd like details on that or any other policy!

There are **two PTO policies** in place, and which one applies to you depends on your employment status. Here's a summary of both:

---

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) *(Full-Time Employees)*

**Scope:** This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their probationary period.[1]

**PTO Accrual (based on years of service):**



| Years of Service | PTO Days per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |

PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

**Key Details:**
- PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]
- Employees may **carry over up to 40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year, with a maximum PTO balance of **240 hours**.[1]
- Employees who separate in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours**.[1]

---

## 📋 Policy 50020 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) – Part-Time Employees

**Scope:** This policy applies to all **regular part-time employees** who work a **minimum of 20 hours per week** and have completed their probationary period.[2]

**PTO Accrual (pro-rated, based on hours worked):**



| Years of Service | Accrual Rate |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 0.0385 hours per hour worked |
| 3–5 years | 0.0577 hours per hour worked |
| 6+ years | 0.0769 hours per hour worked |

[2]

**Key Details:**
- PTO is deducted in **hourly increments** and requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]
- Part-time employees may **carry over up to 20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year.[2]
- Part-time employees who **transition to full-time** status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy.[2]

---

> 💡 **To determine which policy applies to you**, simply identify whether you are a **full-time** or **part-time** employee. If you're unsure of your employment classification, please reach out to your HR department.

Here is a detailed comparison of the full-time and part-time PTO policies:

---

# 📋 PTO Policy Comparison: Full-Time vs. Part-Time

---

## 📌 Policy Overview

| | **Full-Time** | **Part-Time** |
|---|---|---|
| **Policy Number** | Policy 50010 | Policy 50020 |
| **Policy Title** | Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) | Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO) – Part-Time |

---

## 👥 Scope / Eligibility

- **Full-Time:** This policy applies to all regular full-time employees who have completed their probationary period.[1]
- **Part-Time:** This policy applies to all regular part-time employees who work a minimum of 20 hours per week and have completed their probationary period.[2]

---

## ⏱️ PTO Accrual

- **Full-Time:** Full-time employees accrue PTO based on years of service:
  - **0–2 years:** 15 days per year
  - **3–5 years:** 20 days per year
  - **6–10 years:** 25 days per year
  - **11+ years:** 30 days per year

  PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis.[1]

- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees accrue PTO on a pro-rated basis calculated from their regularly scheduled hours. Accrual rates are:
  - **0–2 years:** 0.0385 hours per hour worked
  - **3–5 years:** 0.0577 hours per hour worked
  - **6+ years:** 0.0769 hours per hour worked[2]

---

## 📅 Usage & Scheduling

- **Full-Time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Employees must request PTO through the designated time-off system. Requests for three or more consecutive days require supervisor approval at least two weeks in advance.[1]
- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees must request PTO in accordance with their regular schedule. PTO is deducted in hourly increments. Requests must be submitted through the time-off system.[2]

---

## 🔄 Carryover

- **Full-Time:** Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. Maximum PTO balance at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual stops when the maximum balance is reached.[1]
- **Part-Time:** Part-time employees may carry over up to **20 hours** of unused PTO per calendar year. Accrual stops when maximum balance is reached.[2]

---

## 💼 PTO at Separation

- **Full-Time:** Employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]
- **Part-Time:** Policy 50020 does **not** specify a PTO payout provision upon separation.

---

## 🔁 Eligibility Changes

- Part-time employees who transition to full-time status will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy (Policy 50010).[2]

---

## 🔑 Key Differences at a Glance

| Feature | Full-Time (Policy 50010) | Part-Time (Policy 50020) |
|---|---|---|
| **Accrual Method** | Days per year (fixed tiers) | Hours per hour worked (pro-rated) |
| **Max Carryover** | 40 hours | 20 hours |
| **Max Balance** | 240 hours | Not specified |
| **Separation Payout** | Up to 80 hours | Not specified |
| **Consecutive Days Rule** | Yes (2-week advance notice) | Not specified |

---

> 💡 **Note:** For questions about your specific PTO balance or eligibility, please consult the time-off system or contact HR directly.

---

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
This policy is designed to provide **income protection** for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.[1]

### Scope / Eligibility
This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

### Claim Process
Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]

---

> ⚠️ *Please note that this is a summary of HR policy information and does not constitute legal advice. For specific questions about your situation, please contact Human Resources directly.*

## 📋 Policy 10000 — Code of Ethics and Related Matters

### 🎯 Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to establish standards of ethical conduct for all employees and ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.[1]

---

### 👥 Scope
This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

---

All employees are expected to conduct themselves with **integrity, honesty, and professionalism** in all business dealings. Employees must avoid conflicts of interest and disclose any potential conflicts to their supervisor or the Ethics Committee.[1]

---

Employees must not engage in activities that conflict with the interests of the organization. This includes:
- Financial interests in competing businesses

---

### 🔍 Compliance and Enforcement
Violations of this Code of Ethics may result in **disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment**. The Ethics Committee is responsible for investigating reported violations and recommending appropriate corrective action.[1]

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### Purpose & Scope
The purpose of this policy is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. It applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have **completed their probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏳ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, on a **per-pay-period basis**, as follows:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|-----------------|-------------------|
| 0–2 years       | 15 days           |
| 3–5 years       | 20 days           |
| 6–10 years      | 25 days           |
| 11+ years       | 30 days           |
[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval **at least two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 📦 Carryover & Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over **up to 40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops once that maximum is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for **unused accrued PTO**, up to a maximum of **80 hours**, at their **current rate of pay**.[1]

---

- **Full-time:** PTO may be used for vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

- **Full-time** employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The maximum PTO balance at any time is **240 hours**, and accrual stops when this maximum is reached.[1]

- **Full-time** employees who separate from employment in good standing will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]
- **Part-time:** Policy 50020 does **not** address PTO payout at separation.

- Part-time employees who transition to **full-time status** will have their PTO balance converted and begin accruing under the full-time PTO policy (Policy 50010).[2]

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to provide **income protection** for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability.[1]

### Eligibility (Scope)
This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches the maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

### Claim Process
Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]

This policy applies to all full-time, part-time, and temporary employees of the organization.[1]

Violations of this Code of Ethics may result in **disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment**. The Ethics Committee is responsible for investigating reported violations and recommending appropriate corrective action.[1]

## 📋 Policy 50010 — Types of Leave: Paid Time Off (PTO)

### 🎯 Purpose & Scope
The purpose of Policy 50010 is to establish the Paid Time Off (PTO) policy for eligible full-time employees. This policy applies to all **regular full-time employees** who have completed their **probationary period**.[1]

---

### ⏳ PTO Accrual
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on **years of service**, as follows:

| Years of Service | PTO Days Per Year |
|---|---|
| 0–2 years | 15 days |
| 3–5 years | 20 days |
| 6–10 years | 25 days |
| 11+ years | 30 days |

PTO accrues on a **per-pay-period basis**.[1]

---

### 🗓️ PTO Usage
PTO may be used for **vacation, personal time, illness, or any other purpose**. Employees must request PTO through the **designated time-off system**. Requests for **three or more consecutive days** require supervisor approval at least **two weeks in advance**.[1]

---

### 🔄 Carryover & Maximum Balance
Employees may carry over up to **40 hours** of unused PTO to the following calendar year. The **maximum PTO balance** at any time is **240 hours**. Accrual **stops** when the maximum balance is reached.[1]

---

### 💼 PTO at Separation
Employees who separate from employment **in good standing** will be paid for unused accrued PTO up to a maximum of **80 hours** at their current rate of pay.[1]

---

The policy that covers time away from work due to being temporarily unable to work is **Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability**. Here is a summary of the key details:

---

## 📋 Policy 50030 — Short-Term Disability

### Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to provide **income protection for eligible employees who are unable to work due to a qualifying short-term disability**.[1]

---

### Scope
This policy applies to **all regular full-time employees** who have completed **90 days of continuous employment**.[1]

---

### Benefit Amount
Eligible employees receive **60% of their base weekly salary** during an approved short-term disability period, subject to a maximum weekly benefit. Benefits begin after a **seven (7) calendar day elimination period**.[1]

---

### Duration of Benefits
Short-term disability benefits are payable for **up to 26 weeks** per disability period. Benefits cease when the employee is able to return to work, reaches maximum benefit duration, or qualifies for long-term disability.[1]

---

### Qualifying Conditions
Short-term disability covers **non-work-related injuries and illnesses** that prevent the employee from performing the essential functions of their position. Work-related injuries are covered under **Workers' Compensation**.[1]

---

### Claim Process
Employees must **notify their supervisor and Human Resources within three (3) business days** of the onset of disability. A completed claim form and supporting medical documentation must be submitted to the disability administrator **within 15 days**.[1]

---

> 💡 **Note:** If you have any questions about your specific situation or need assistance filing a claim, please contact your HR representative directly.
